prompt_en: Create a photorealistic fantasy field-biologist photograph of an original adult fictional woman whose visible facial appearance and long dark wavy hair are guided by Image 1. At a volcanic plateau observatory above steaming fumaroles, she stands beside a calibrated range pole and records two separate creatures in one wide frame. The photograph contains the woman, one wyvern, and one hydra as three clearly separated living subjects. Use a raised wide documentary viewpoint: her face stays readable near center while both creatures remain uncropped, full-body, and large enough to inspect every limb and neck junction. On a basalt ledge, show a two-legged winged wyvern topology in an elevated three-quarter landing view: one head neck torso and pelvis form one coherent creature body; exactly two wings connect symmetrically near the shoulders; exactly two weight-bearing hind legs descend from the pelvis; no separate foreleg pair appears beneath or beside the wings; one long tail continues from the pelvis without branching. Farther downslope, show a grounded single-body multi-neck hydra: one torso pelvis and limb system anchors every neck; three or more complete neck paths remain visible from torso to head; each neck has a distinct non-merged root on the same shoulder system; each head retains a separate silhouette jaw and orientation; feet body shadow and nearby objects preserve one coherent creature scale. Her tablet, range pole, creature contact shadows, and wind-displaced ash make the survey action and shared scale immediately legible. Cold dawn side light crosses all three subjects from one direction, separating wing membranes, leg attachments, neck roots, and grounded shadows. Preserve the reference-visible facial structure, hairline, dark wavy hair texture, and natural makeup balance. Image 1 supplies visible-appearance guidance only for this original adult fictional woman.
